title: Is this better?
author: NightwoodStudios
selftext:
I made a post a few days ago getting feedback on the game I have been working on. The few comments I got was that it looked too much like obvious AI art with no real style. I liked the style but it was a valid criticism. I have been reworking the game to see what other styles that I like might work better and not look so offensively AI. This is a style I really gel with and think could fit the game well. Does this stand out as AI or lack personality?

This is all being done in ChatGPT Codex. I have found it very good at following the style guides I give it but I am struggling to figure out exactly what does and doesn't put people of when it comes to looking looking like AI. Definitely one of the harder parts of the whole game dev process. Any other thoughts on this would be good to know.

  
This is my game if anyone would like to see the current style and maybe wish list it: [Into The Nightwood](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5528540/Into_The_Nightwood/)

comments.author: KS-Wolf-1978
comments.body:
"ChatGPT"

It has its own style which people will instantly recognize, so if it is important to you to avoid getting the "obvious AI art" comments, just use anything else.

I dislike it for two big reasons:

1. Too many unnecessary details the existence of doesn't make any artistic sense.

2. It literally can not do good pixel art (i am old enough to remember the first coming of pixelart - Atari, Amiga, PC with 320×240 256 colors VGA and glowing blobs for pixels on a CRT, not perfect squares).

Solution:

Get a GPU with at least 16GB VRAM and go local with ComfyUI and few of the newest most liked free models.

https://github.com/Tavris1/ComfyUI-Easy-Install

Krea 2, Qwen 2.1, Flux 2 Klein, Moss and the old but still good Flux Fill OneReward.

Also ask your AI to suggest you some freebie pixel art editing software, so you can manually fix small problems when needed.

comments.author: AnimalPowers
comments.body:
Try this.  Put down the keyboard.  get a piece of paper and pencil.  Draw.    Then “reprompt your brain” and draw a different style.   Keep reprompting your brain until you run out of brain tokens.    Then, after your brain limit resets prompt some more.   You should have a stack of papers.     

take the papers and stare at them.  Prompt your heart for emotions.    Continue staring at the drawings you drew in real life until you run out of heart tokens.   Repeat until your weekly heart usage is up.  

take the winning image and give it to chatgpt.

comments.author: Fairway3Games
comments.body:
Ask for medium level of detail or less. Especially for the background.

The background, frame, art, etc all have the same colors. There's no contrast. There's no separation.

You have a strong red/purple AND (impressively in a bad way) yellow/brown filter on everything. That's painful on the eyes.

There's a strange perspective effect, but it hurts to look at since it was done without implementing it correctly.

comments.author: frankenstein-0x00e
comments.body:
Ask your AI model to research game design, clarity and color theories

this communicates nothing but noise to the player

background should be made of Chunks of textured spots that dont attract attention

Characters should be less detailed for this profile view, silhouette focused rather than details, ideally a solid color background that reflects the typa of character (ex: red attack focused hero, green tank focused hero, blue / purple magic)

the background's perspective makes no sense, use references like TFT (teamfight tactics) board or similar card fighting games

  
references are great to learn from for YOU as well, its not art style but rather the hidden rules of game design in references

dont rush building, have a coffee with Claude to breakdown few screenshots of other games and why they work then turn these into md files that your builder agent can follow

  
this is where your effort comes in. You need to develop an eye for aesthetics and game feel
